title: Token approvals explained, and how to revoke them
seoTitle: Token Approvals Explained: How to Revoke Them | CRYPY
description: Apps you used may still be allowed to spend your tokens. Learn what a token approval is, when it becomes dangerous, and how to check and revoke yours.
summary: Every app you used may still be allowed to spend your tokens. How to find and remove them.
inShort: An approval lets a contract move one of your tokens without asking you again.
It stays active until you remove it, even after you stop using the app.
Removing one is a small transaction you confirm in your own wallet.

blocks.text: Before an exchange or other app can move a token from your wallet, you give it permission once. That permission is the approval: it names the contract (the **spender**) and how much of the token it may move.

blocks.caption: An approval is a standing permission. The tokens stay in your wallet until the contract uses it.
blocks.alt: Your wallet gives an exchange contract permission to spend an unlimited amount of USDT.

blocks.text: For NFTs there is a wider version: **approve for all**, which lets the spender move every NFT you hold in that collection.

Many apps ask for an unlimited amount so you don't have to approve again next time. If that contract is later hacked, or was malicious from the start, it can move all of that token from your wallet, including tokens you receive later.
Approvals are also the target of many phishing sites: a fake page asks you to "claim" or "verify" something, and the transaction you confirm is really an approval for the scammer's contract.
Revoking is never needed to "unlock" or "verify" a wallet. A site or message that says so, or that asks for your seed phrase, is a scam.

Paste your wallet address into the [Approval Checker](tool:approval-checker). It looks for approvals on Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum and Polygon, reads each one on-chain, and puts the ones that need attention first: unknown contracts, unlimited amounts and spenders flagged by security data.
Checking doesn't need your wallet: anyone can look up any address, because approvals are public.

items: Open the [Approval Checker](tool:approval-checker) and check your address, or connect your wallet and check it. Connecting never asks you to sign.
Look at **Needs attention** first, and decide which approvals you no longer need.
Click **Revoke** next to one. CRYPY tests the transaction first and shows what it does and the fee.
Check the details in your wallet and confirm. Once the transaction is in a block, the allowance is zero.

blocks.text: Revoking sets the allowance to zero. Your tokens don't move.

Approvals for apps you use often, ideally limited to the amount you trade, are normal. Revoking them only means you approve again, and pay a fee, next time. Focus on approvals for apps you no longer use, contracts you don't recognize, and unlimited approvals on tokens worth a lot.

faq.a: Yes, a small network fee, because revoking is a blockchain transaction.
No. It only removes the permission. Your tokens stay in your wallet.

faq.q: Can I check without connecting my wallet?
faq.a: Yes. Approvals are public, so you can check any address. Revoking needs your wallet, because only you can change your own permissions.
